chapters.text:
I set out in Coldridge Valley with my kin in mind. A name was worth keeping only if the work behind it stood up. The cold of Dun Morogh caught in my throat, and the pines bowed under their snow. Above the valleys rose the mountain that holds Ironforge, and the sight of it made the cold easier to bear. When I tramped into Anvilmar, I fought wolves for the first time, with fresh respect for what was in their mouths. I handed Tough Wolf Meat over to Sten Stoutarm. Once back in Coldridge Valley, I fought off Burly Rockjaw Troggs and finished off Rockjaw Troggs at Balir Frosthammer's request, the grunting echoing long after; I settled Talin Keeneye's business with Grelin Whitebeard. A Frostmane Troll Whelp got too close to ending things there. I would rather bring my kin a plain account of a mistake than a fine account of my funeral. I dealt with plenty of Frostmane Troll Whelps, quicker on the feet than I had allowed for.

The journal went safely into Grelin Whitebeard's hands. I went on equipped with a Frostmane Leather Belt. Back in Anvilmar, the trainer taught me Serpent Sting and Track Beasts. I delivered a message to Marryk Nurribit.

I had done six tasks by the end. I counted ten Ragged Young Wolves and four Burly Rockjaw Troggs, glad to be using a pen. All told, it had taken an hour and thirty-five minutes. I rested in Anvilmar, glad to put my pack down before it became a permanent part of me.

I was ready to move in Anvilmar. The road was not going to shorten itself out of consideration. I smelled the Thunderbrew Distillery before I had properly reached Kharanos. Smoke rose above the houses, where dwarves and gnomes crowded together against the cold, and I felt my shoulders ease at the sight. My hearthstone was bound at the Thunderbrew Distillery from then on. I began my training in skinning, my hands slower than my pride; I learned the first of leatherworking. I faced boars for the first time, with a healthy respect for their teeth. I delivered a Crag Boar Rib to Ragnar Thunderbrew. I finished a Handstitched Leather Vest. I put on a Handstitched Leather Vest of my own making.

I found my way to the Grizzled Den, curious what the locals would make of a dwarf. I completed Loslor Rudge's errand with Hegnar Rumbleshot. My path led into Brewnall Village. I took a Gyromechanic Gear to Razzle Sprysprocket. My training added Arcane Shot. I spent a rough night in Shimmer Ridge, where the thought of a proper rest grew more attractive by the hour.

I woke in Shimmer Ridge and put my pack in order before going on. I killed Timber there, glad to have something to report that would stand up to a second telling. I improved my skinning to fifty, still a long way from a master's bench. A Frostmane Scepter was among the spoils, a rare thing.

The road brought me to Frostmane Hold. I agreed to explore Frostmane Hold, and did. I arrived in Amberstill Ranch, keen to put a place to the name. I saw to Vagash for Rudra Amberstill, my beard none the worse, which was the main thing.

In Kharanos again, I came away from training with Raptor Strike. With Hunter's Mark, nothing I had marked could hide from me.

I counted five jobs done, glad that I could put a proper ending to what people had asked of me. Of the fighting, eleven Leper Gnomes and ten Frostmane Snowstriders made up the most. The stretch had taken two hours and a half. I settled in Kharanos, with the work done well enough that it could wait without worrying me.

I made ready in Kharanos, giving my gear the sort of look that saves trouble later. When I tramped on to the Grizzled Den, I saw a Wendigo Mane safely to Pilot Stonegear. I shared the road with Thorgrim, the walk shorter in company. The way went on into Gol'Bolar Quarry. I brought down several Rockjaw Bonesnappers for Ozzie Togglevolt, harder in the skull than anything had a right to be.

In Kharanos again, I was taught Concussive Shot and Mend Pet. I took the road to Amberstill Ranch, the country on either side worth a second look. I brought Bristle into my care. Grateful for warmth enough to make standing still a pleasure, I stopped at a fire. Bristle fell. Out here, it could as easily have been me.

The blue water of Loch Modan lay still behind the Stonewrought Dam. I knew dwarves built on a grand scale, but the weight of all that water made me stop and look. I reached North Gate Pass. I found the Stoutlager Inn of Thelsamar beside the loch. After the open hills, its ale and blood sausages interested me more than the distance I had come. I made a bed for myself there and tried to put the road out of my thoughts.

I began in Coldridge Valley, with a great many questions and no intention of letting my size set the scale of them. The snow of Dun Morogh glowed blue under the stars, and the lamps in the village windows looked warmer for it. I knew the shapes of those mountains even in the dark. I burned several Rockjaw Troggs for Balir Frosthammer. I had my first encounter with wolves, their jaws best studied from a distance. I delivered Tough Wolf Meat to Sten Stoutarm.

When I set foot in Anvilmar, I added Frost Armor and Arcane Missiles to what I knew. I took the message to Grelin Whitebeard.

I had brought three tasks to an end, rather glad that my help had found a use. Most of the fighting had been against nine Ragged Young Wolves. All told, it had taken forty minutes. I paused in Anvilmar, where doing nothing seemed a perfectly workable arrangement.

I took up the road in Anvilmar, rather pleased that I had not yet run out of things to wonder about. I smelled the Thunderbrew Distillery before I had properly reached Kharanos. Smoke rose above the houses, where dwarves and gnomes crowded together against the cold, and I felt my shoulders ease at the sight. I delivered a message to Tharek Blackstone. My training added Frostbolt. I could conjure water out of nothing now, which settled the question of what to drink on the road. I took to wearing an Apprentice's Robe. I made it as far as Brewnall Village, where I took a Gyromechanic Gear to Razzle Sprysprocket. A Frostmane Headhunter nearly ended me in Frostmane Hold. I had found a flaw in my approach rather more directly than I intended.

book.epitaph: A Frostmane Shadowcaster ended the road of Pippa, a gnome mage, in Frostmane Hold. Level six. One life, as the realm allows. Only the beginning: five tasks, twenty-seven foes. Gnomeregan has lost another of its children.

chapters.text:
I took up the road in Darkshire, with a little curiosity left over from my worrying. I gave my hearthstone a place of return there. I set foot in Raven Hill Cemetery, the road dusty and the company scarce. Skeletal Horrors were down before I thinned out a fair number of Skeletal Fiends for Commander Althea Ebonlock. The road brought me to Brightwood Grove. I took my hammer to several Nightbane Shadow Weavers for Calor, my heart still going when the fight was over; I added a Night Watch Shortsword to my equipment.

Once back in Darkshire, I studied Seal of Command and Holy Light. With Hammer of Justice, the Light could stop a foe in its tracks. I walked into the Hushed Bank, interested in who might need a hand here. I completed the errand from Madame Eva to Abercrombie. I died in Raven Hill, leaving more unfinished than I had known how to worry about.

That made three tasks in all. My tally came to three Skeletal Horrors. The stretch had taken an hour and fifteen minutes; I was ready to put my pack down. I stopped in Darkshire. For once I could look about without looking for the way out.

I began this stretch in Darkshire, hoping the day would be kinder than the last. The way went on into Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. I carried a Ghoul Rib to Abercrombie. I slept outside, wishing I had found a softer place to lie.

book.prologue: I should have started this journal long ago. I have done eighty-seven good turns already, and I'm writing this in Duskwood.

chapters.text:
I began in the Valley of Trials, where strength would have to serve a purpose beyond proving that I had it. Heat rose from the red dust of Durotar, as if the ground itself were breathing. This was the land we had claimed, and I meant to learn how to belong to it. I thinned out several Mottled Boars for Gornek, fast, but not fast enough. I finished Sarkoth off at Hana'zua's asking, over in a few hard blows. Zureetha Fargaze needed Vile Familiars thinned out, so I thinned them.

The rest of it was smaller work, the kind that fills a day without being noticed. A Cactus Apple went safely into Galgar's hands. I obliged Foreman Thazz'ril. At Razor Hill I heard the forge before I saw the drilling. Beyond the barracks, Kul Tiras ships sat off the coast, and I understood why no one in the town ever quite stood at rest. I completed Gornek's errand with Master Gadrin. My training added Rend and Battle Shout. I fitted myself with a Rough Leather Vest. A Kul Tiras Marine nearly ended me. Pride had asked more of my strength than sense would have allowed. One more errand was seen to besides. I dealt with Scorpid Workers first and finished off Kul Tiras Sailors at Gar'Thok's request, each one met head on.

I had finished eight tasks. Nine Scorpid Workers had fallen to me over the stretch. After an hour and forty-five minutes, I could put the day's deeds in order and look plainly at what they had taught me. I settled in Razor Hill, glad to have work behind me that needed no excuse.

I began again in Razor Hill. What was asked of me deserved an answer in deeds. The drums of Orgrimmar echoed off the spiked walls as I came in. At Grommash Hold I felt the weight of it: a city our people had built for themselves, with no one's chains on it. The road brought me to the Valley of Strength. I came away knowing Thunder Clap, strength given a better shape. With Charge, the distance between me and a foe stopped mattering. I took the message to Gor the Enforcer. I slept on the ground, where the day's work gave me reason enough to rest.

I began in Shadowglen, where the world beyond familiar paths had become impossible to leave to others. Moonlight silvered the leaves of Teldrassil while owls called overhead. I listened between my footfalls, unwilling to hurry through so much quiet. I encountered boars at close quarters, fierce in the way of all things that must eat. Young Thistle Boars fell to me before I turned the wild's wrath on Young Nightsabers for Conservator Ilthalaine. I delivered a message to Mardant Strongoak. I thinned out Grells for Tarindrella, the reek of the Nether hanging about the place. I had my first encounter with spiders, understanding them a little better in the end.

I handed a Webwood Venom Sac over to Gilshalan Windwalker. The trainer taught me Moonfire and Rejuvenation. Rain scented the houses around the moonwell in Dolanaar. The sentinels kept their patient watch on the road, and I let my guard down a little. I carried a message on to Iverron. I bedded down, glad of room enough to be still for a while.

I rose in Dolanaar after the rough night's rest, with the path still waiting. I made sure a Nightsaber Pelt reached Zenn Foulhoof and brought an Emerald Dreamcatcher to Tallonkai Swiftroot. I swapped a piece or two of my gear.

I had seen seven tasks through, and knew more of the people who had asked them of me. Most of it had been against eleven Webwood Spiders and four Nightsabers. All of it had taken an hour and twenty-five minutes. I paused in Dolanaar, where stillness brought back what haste had let me overlook.

I took up the path in Dolanaar, looking first for what had changed while my attention was elsewhere. The white stone and still pools of Darnassus slowed me without my meaning to. Near the Temple of the Moon the old hush settled around me, and I was home. I came to the Temple of the Moon. I did what Mathrengyl Bearwalker asked of me. I rested with the sky above me, glad of the pause in my journey.

I began in Deathknell, with my own hand on the page and no master's will behind it. A modest distinction, until one has lived without it. Crows called over the crypts of Tirisfal, toward the broken walls of Lordaeron. Night changed little here, though it left me feeling less conspicuous. Then came the everyday work, the sort every place has more of than hands for. I carried a message on to Shadow Priest Sarvis. With several Wretched Zombies cut down along the way, I smote Mindless Zombies with the Light, the cold lingering on my hands. I brought down Young Night Web Spiders for Executor Arren and put Scavenged Goods into Deathguard Saltain's hands.

A Scarlet Armband was in Executor Arren's hands soon after. I took instruction in Shadow Word: Pain. Power Word: Shield was a ward of light to take the blows meant for me. After the tombs, the crooked roofs of Brill looked almost companionable. Around the Gallows' End Tavern my people went about their business, and the town kept going on stubbornness alone. I made sure a Tirisfal Pumpkin reached Apothecary Johaan. I dealt with Maggot Eye for Executor Zygand, my own pulse, had I one, unbothered; I added a Lightweight Chain Robe to my equipment.

The tasks came to seven, the last for Executor Zygand. The fighting came to twelve Scarlet Converts and eight Wretched Zombies. I had spent an hour and fifty minutes on the road, choosing what to do with it. That part was worth recording. I settled in Brill, where being still was a choice rather than a condition imposed on me.

I set out in Brill, where usefulness remained a more reliable introduction than appearance. Green canals ran past the bubbling Apothecarium, deep beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Out of so much that had survived badly, we had made a city, and it was ours. My path led into the Trade Quarter. I took lessons in Mind Blast. Renew was a healing that kept on working long after the prayer was done. A Vile Fin Scale went safely into Master Apothecary Faranell's hands. I passed the night without much sleep, though I was glad enough to be still.

Glad to be moving again, I set out in the Dwarven District. I flew from Stormwind to Sentinel Hill, glad to see how the places fitted together from above.

Westfall lay dark and quiet, its windmills turning over farms nobody tended any more. A light in a window was rare enough to make me wonder who still dared to keep one. A stone tower stood on Sentinel Hill, and around it the People's Militia had pitched their tents. Farmers who had lost everything queued for soup, and it made me angrier than I expected. A Mysterious Message was in Gryan Stoutmantle's hands soon after. Moonbrook was a ruin after dark, its broken walls black against the sky. Somewhere among the burned houses the Defias were talking, and I kept to the shadows. I helped the Defias Traitor as I had promised. In Sentinel Hill again, I reported back once more. Thessaly, Brannigan, Rowan and Halvard joined me.

Defias Pillagers, a Defias Highwayman, several Undead Excavators and a few Undead Dynamiters kept me busy while I had a handful of Miners' Union Cards in my pack, with an ache in my back for my trouble. After a fight with Foreman Thistlenettle, I found Thistlenettle's Badge.

Mine carts stood abandoned on their rails, and the walls sweated in the lamplight. The deeper I went into the Deadmines, the louder the hammering grew. Rhahk'Zor did not survive the fight. After a fight or two with Defias Miners, Defias Overseers, Rhahk'Zor, Defias Taskmasters, Defias Evokers, Goblin Woodcarvers, Goblin Craftsmen and a Sneed's Shredder, I collected a Gnoam Sprecklesprocket, with no wish to lose the find on the way back. It was Sneed's turn to fall. Gilnid was the next to fall. Sea air reached me before I saw the cove. A great ironclad ship sat in the hidden harbour, its decks crowded with pirates, and I could hardly believe it had been built underground.

With Defias Pirates, Defias Companions and Defias Squallshapers cut down along the way, I recovered Red Silk Bandanas, enough of them to fill a sack, nearly. Mr. Smite nearly finished me in Ironclad Cove. My hands went on shaking after there was any need for them to move. Mr. Smite fell at last. After I came by Smite's Mighty Hammer, I had it in use before long. I saw the end of Captain Greenskin. Edwin VanCleef fell, and my business in the Deadmines was over. I was almost afraid to let the relief reach me. I had Mr. Smite, Defias Blackguards, Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef to deal with before I claimed VanCleef's head as proof of the deed. I brought down Cookie.

Gryan Stoutmantle had my report soon after. I equipped Chausses of Westfall and ran one more errand. I left Sentinel Hill by air for Stormwind, with a little of the day's hurry falling away beneath me.

Smaller jobs came next, one on the heels of the other. I came to Cathedral Square, the road dusty and the company scarce. I brought an Unsent Letter to Baros Alexston; I handed in my work to Wilder Thistlenettle and Shoni the Shilent.

The road brought me to Old Town. I trained in Cleave and Retaliation, keen to find out how much had stayed with me.

I had seen eight tasks to their end. My tally came to eight Defias Miners and six Defias Pirates. I had spent two hours and a half travelling, and felt the distance when I stopped. I rested in the Trade District, glad to think back over the road instead of keeping pace with it.
I set out in the Trade District, wondering whose doorstep the day's work would bring me to. I bedded down there, with the sounds around me taking longer to grow familiar than I liked.

book.prologue: I should have started this journal long ago. I have done sixty-four good turns already, and I'm writing this in Stormwind City.
